summary_en: This study tests transoral robotic surgery (TORS) alone for HPV-related oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma in patients whose HPV circulating tumor DNA is undetectable after surgery. The treatment is robotic surgical removal of the tumor through the mouth, and how long or how often it is given is not stated. The study aims to determine whether cancer control and survival are comparable to those reported with standard therapy, and it is a Phase 2 trial.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa la cirugía robótica transoral (TORS) sola para el carcinoma de células escamosas de orofaringe relacionado con VPH, en pacientes cuyo ADN tumoral circulante de VPH es indetectable después de la cirugía. El tratamiento consiste en la extirpación quirúrgica robótica del tumor a través de la boca, y no se indica cuánto tiempo ni con qué frecuencia se administra. El estudio busca determinar si el control del cáncer y la supervivencia son comparables a los reportados con la terapia estándar, y es un ensayo de Fase 2.
who_for: Resectable p16-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, early or intermediate stage without distant spread
Detectable pre-surgery HPV circulating tumor DNA (at least 10 fragments/mL)
Undetectable HPV circulating tumor DNA after surgery (under 5 fragments/mL)
Age 18 or older with ECOG performance status 0 or 1
Adequate blood counts and kidney function; no active smoking in past 5 years and under 20 pack-years
not_for: Advanced nodal stage, unresectable disease, or unequivocal distant metastases
Non-high-risk HPV subtype, or p16- or HPV-negative cancer
5 or more positive lymph nodes on final pathology
Detectable HPV circulating tumor DNA (over 5 fragments/mL) 1 to 5 weeks after surgery
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or concurrent anti-cancer therapy
